overview.description: Kujong (known in Belgium as Couillon) is a fast-paced trick-taking card game popular in the Low Countries (Belgium, Netherlands) and parts of Germany and Luxembourg. Played by four players in two fixed teams, it uses a 24-card deck. The game is known for its 'erasing' scoring system, where teams start with a 'tree' of 10-12 branches and aim to be the first to prune their tree to zero by winning rounds.

history.origins: Dates to the 19th century as a simplified variant of the French Jass and Belote families. The name 'Couillon' is Walloon French slang; in Flemish regions, it is often called 'Kwajongen' or 'Troeven'.
timeline: 1890s: Couillon variants become standard in Belgian cafes.
1940s: 'Kujong' emerges as a localized phonetic name in some Eastern Belgian and border regions.
Present: A very common 'Kroegspel' (pub game) and family game in the Benelux region.
history.evolution: The game evolved to use a very small deck (24 cards) to ensure high-rank clashes in every hand.
history.cultural: In Belgium, the loser is traditionally 'traktatie' (must buy the next round of drinks).

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (A+C vs B+D).
setup.deck: 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9 in four suits. Ace is highest (4 pts), King (3), Queen (2), Jack (1).
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 3 cards initially. The next card is turned up for the Trump suit. After the suit is accepted or rejected, each player gets 3 more cards.

rules.objective: Win more points in tricks than the other team to 'erase' a branch from your score tree.
rules.gameplay:
1. Must follow suit. If unable, play any card (or Trump).
2. Highest Trump wins, or highest card of the led suit.
3. **Points**: Trick capture is based on rank (A-K-Q-J-10-9). Point cards in the entire deck total 40.
keyRules: 24-card deck: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9 in four suits
Must win at least 21 points to erase a branch

strategy.basic: Prioritize the Aces. Holding two Aces in a 6-card hand makes you nearly guaranteed to capture at least 10 points. If your partner also holds an Ace, you have 20 pointsâ€”just one point shy of winning the round.
strategy.intermediate: Trump Defensive: If the opponent chooses trumps, lead low cards in your 'longest' suit to force them to use their trump cards early. If you can exhaust their 6 trump cards, your remaining Aces becomes masters.
strategy.advanced: The 'Kapot' Strategy: If your team has high cards in all suits, aim for 'Kapot' (winning all 6 tricks). This erases multiple branches (usually 2 or 3) and is the fastest path to victory.
tips: Always watch which player 'Accepted' the Trump. They are the target for all your defensive leads.
In Kujong, the Queen of Spades (De Mit) is the 'Joker' of the deckâ€”don't lose her to a low Jack.

difficulty.easy: Fails to reach 21 points; ignores partners' leads; poor trump choices.
difficulty.medium: Reasonable trump selection; basic point counting (aiming for 21).
difficulty.hard: Expert at 'Kapot' detection; perfectly manages the 24-card deck memory; uses 'Mit' strategy effectively.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.
